clue.text: Nares troubled with her fire — what can get rid of nasty smell?

definitions.text: what can get rid of nasty smell?

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so the letters of these three words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's nostrils are bothered by her fire, and they want something to clear the bad smell.
explanation.walkthrough: Nares is the anatomical word for nostrils, which makes the smell picture neat; here it is only letters to be rearranged with HER and FIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: This household spray or device is designed to mask or remove unpleasant odours in a room.

clue.text: Troublemaker finishing, coming any minute?

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little troublemaker
finishing as a noun is an ending

explanation.surface: A troublemaker is about to wrap up, and someone wonders if it will be soon.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impending is about to happen, so it may arrive at any moment now.

clue.text: Female, one with extraordinary sense and diplomacy

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests something out of its usual form, so the letters of sense are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman with remarkable perception and tact is being praised.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is delicate skill in handling people or situations, the tact a diplomat needs.

clue.text: Runs to get optional items?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, runs not scored off the bat (byes, wides
second meaning: add-ons you may choose to pay for

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, runs added to the score from byes, wides and no-balls rather than from the bat are recorded as extras.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both cricket's bonus runs and additional features offered beyond the basic package.

clue.text: Part of body buried in rich earth

indicators.note: buried in says the letters lie concealed inside the words rich earth

explanation.surface: Some part of a body has been buried in fertile soil, a grisly garden scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart is the organ in the chest that pumps blood around the body.

clue.text: Food vessel capsized

indicators.note: capsized means turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the word backwards

parts.note: a tun is a large cask, a vessel for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A ship carrying food has overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: Vessel suggests a boat to go with capsized, but here it is a tun, a big barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A nut is an edible kernel in a hard shell, a common item of food.

clue.text: Daughter is entering rally, getting to turn up again

indicators.note: entering says D and IS go inside the word for rally

parts.note: to rally after illness is to recover

explanation.surface: A daughter joins a rally and manages to show up once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To rediscover something is to find it again, to make it turn up a second time.

clue.text: Old writer accessible to all

parts.note: a pen is an instrument for writing

explanation.surface: An elderly author is available to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer suggests a person, but it is the pen that writes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open is unrestricted, available for anyone to enter or use.

clue.text: Like someone being celebrated getting browned off?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person whose health is drunk at a party has been ...
second meaning: bread browned under a grill; the question mark flags that browned off normally means fed up

explanation.walkthrough: Browned off is British slang for fed up, which would be an odd thing for a celebrated person to be; the phrase is read literally as cooked brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising glasses in honour of someone, or grilling bread until golden, both use the same verb.

clue.text: Conventional mother at home with awkward master

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother
in means at home, as in staying in

indicators.note: awkward suggests something clumsy or out of shape, so the letters of master are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traditional mother is at home with a clumsy schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Mainstream as an adjective describes ordinary, widely accepted ideas or tastes, the opposite of fringe.

clue.text: Am I sane, sadly forgetting things?

indicators.note: sadly here means in a sorry state, so the letters of am I sane are scrambled

explanation.surface: A confused person asks whether they are still sane as their memory fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, a condition in which past events are forgotten.

clue.text: Periods when male is restricted by obligations

indicators.note: is restricted by says the male letter is held within the word for obligations

parts.note: ties are bonds or obligations, as in family ties

explanation.surface: There are moments when a man feels hemmed in by his duties.
explanation.definitionFit: Times are spans or eras of history, so the word is a plural synonym for periods.

clue.text: Undertaker could be romantic, I fancy!

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamental, so the letters of romantic and I are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a funeral director might be a romantic type.
explanation.walkthrough: I fancy reads as I think, but fancy is the anagram signal and I is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortician is the American word for a funeral director, the person who prepares the dead.

clue.text: Knight wasn't well attached somehow

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
ailed means was ill

explanation.surface: A knight who was sick has somehow been fastened in place.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailed means fixed with nails, fastened to something; somehow allows for the method.

clue.text: Foreign city left with zero protection either side

indicators.note: protection either side says the zero letters guard the word for left at both ends

parts.note: zero is the letter O, used once on each side, giving two of them
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone left a foreign city with no protection on either flank.
explanation.walkthrough: OPORTO is the old English name for Porto, Portugal's second city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oporto is a major city in Portugal, so to an English solver it is a city abroad.

clue.text: Crazy finish set up in German city

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means raised, so the combined word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: mad means crazy
to stop is to finish

explanation.surface: A wild ending has been arranged in a city in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Potsdam is a city near Berlin, capital of the German state of Brandenburg.

clue.text: Criminal gang with modern technology

parts.note: a band is a group or gang of people
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A criminal gang equips itself with up-to-date gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber or outlaw, especially one in an armed gang.

clue.text: Mean to get one over the eight

definitions.meaning: second meaning: British slang for slightly drunk, having had one drink more than eight pints

explanation.walkthrough: One over the eight is an old British phrase for being tipsy; tight is also slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both miserly with money and somewhat intoxicated after drinking.

clue.text: Tease family member after short time

indicators.note: after says the relative comes following the short time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A relative pokes fun at someone after only a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt someone is to provoke or mock them, a harsher form of teasing.

clue.text: With legs apart in a street journey

parts.note: a ride is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: Someone takes a trip down a road with legs spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting astride means straddling, one leg on each side, as on a horse.

clue.text: Elaborate old lover needing money

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
a pound is a unit of British money

explanation.surface: A former partner who needs cash, described in great detail.
explanation.walkthrough: Elaborate looks like an adjective, but here it is the verb meaning to explain at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to set out and explain in detail, to elaborate on a subject.

clue.text: The old man's dancing step

parts.note: the old man is a familiar term for one's father, pa
the apostrophe-s of man's is kept as S

explanation.surface: Father shows off his dancing move.
explanation.definitionFit: Pas is the ballet term for a step, as in pas de deux.

clue.text: Platform said to be wobbly

indicators.note: wobbly means unsteady or shaky, so the letters of said are jumbled

explanation.surface: A stage is reported to be unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: Said to be looks like a sound-alike signal, but said is the fodder and wobbly rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised stage at one end of a hall for speakers or dignitaries.

clue.text: Smitten mates put out inaccurate bit of information

indicators.note: put out means disturbed or upset, so the letters of smitten and mates are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lovestruck friends are annoyed by a false report.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstatement is an incorrect or misleading claim, a piece of wrong information.
